title: Connected room silent answer
symptom: The room connects and captions update, but the caller hears no returned audio from the agent.
first_check: Trace one turn through TTS output, publication, subscription, inbound packets, decoding, audio element state and output device.
handling: Diagnostic pattern: isolate the failed media stage; existing evidence separates generated text, SDK playout and browser playback observations.
avoid: Do not regenerate business work or claim successful playback because captions, a waveform or a connected badge appear.

title: First scripted voice turn disappears
symptom: Text works, but the first scripted voice turn produces no transcript after the SDK clears its user turn.
first_check: Inspect real AgentSession stream replacement order and count active plus closing STT handles during clear_user_turn.
handling: Implemented: retain two bounded recognizer handles for replacement overlap; the genuine SDK regression still rejects a third handle.
avoid: Do not equate one logical speaker with one instantaneous resource handle or relax the bound without understanding replacement lifetime.

title: Real providers stall before usage
symptom: Configured real providers report zero inference usage while the spoken response times out during a qualification attempt.
first_check: Check native TLS diagnostics, trusted inference mode and whether the explicitly selected approved certificate bundle reached the native runtime.
handling: Supported setup: select the approved certificate-only bundle and rerun P1-20; the current post-v5 provider requalification remains open.
avoid: Do not disable TLS verification, expose provider keys or infer actual inference from a healthy process or configured badge.

title: The inner timeout wins
symptom: Accept fails near two seconds even though the enclosing dispatch step allows five seconds and the original operation later exists.
first_check: Inventory bridge, client, endpoint and claim budgets; compare their actual cutoff times before interpreting the lost acknowledgement.
handling: Implemented joined fix: pass the bridge budget into ExternalOperationClient; new joined profiles separately retain a longer claim lease.
avoid: Do not enlarge only the outer timer, multiply independent retries or treat timeout as proof that acceptance never committed.

title: Signed SMS rejected by time checks
symptom: A correctly shaped SMS request is rejected despite an apparently valid signature and familiar sender identity.
first_check: Check canonical timestamp representation, seconds units, clock skew and the sixty-second transport window before inspecting durable sender association.
handling: Implemented: authenticate bounded raw bytes and canonical transport time, then repeat the protected freshness check after locks. A retry preserves original event semantics while refreshing permitted transport authentication.
avoid: Do not widen the window silently, trust body scope or confuse provider HMAC authentication with customer account authorization.

title: An old interrupt stops new speech
symptom: A delayed interruption or recognition callback affects the next answer instead of the response or source turn that created it.
first_check: Compare immutable response tickets, actual speech handles and caller-bound turn IDs across each await and SDK replacement.
handling: Implemented: interrupt the original bound handle and freeze genuine final recognition before awaiting durable intake; preserve separate business cancellation.
avoid: Do not select mutable current speech after an await or treat stopping agent audio as cancelling accepted supplier work.

title: A grant expires behind a lock
symptom: A worker starts while its lease is live, waits for admission and reaches its protected write after expiry.
first_check: Observe the actual SQL lock wait and sample PostgreSQL time after locks; compare the retained owner, epoch and expiry.
handling: Implemented: use clock_timestamp after lock admission and reject expired authority; native bindings similarly recheck current grant time under protection.
avoid: Do not authorize writes from transaction-start timestamps, cached expiry or worker wall time, even when the epoch still matches.

title: Cancellation cannot prove prevention
symptom: A takeover lookup finds nothing, but an older reserved supplier request may still execute after cancellation or deadline.
first_check: Inspect original dispatch_count, reservation identity and supplier capabilities before interpreting a lookup miss as evidence of nonexecution.
handling: Implemented audit repair: retain UNCERTAIN with ambiguous_outcome when prior dispatch remains possible; cancellation requested remains a separate disposition.
avoid: Do not erase a possible old call, invent a new supplier key or promise reversal from a newer database lease.

title: Valid JSON unsupported conclusion
symptom: The specialist returns a well-formed result that contradicts supplied policy facts or claims an unsupported eligibility conclusion.
first_check: Check exact request and result bindings, policy version and independently validated factual support before considering current applicability.
handling: Implemented: validate factual support before expiry classification and retain only the contractually permitted result; exact human confirmation remains separate.
avoid: Do not promote schema validity, model confidence or a plausible citation into factual truth, current applicability or mutation permission.

title: One click becomes two inputs
symptom: Repeated Send or Enter creates duplicate background work before the first durable acceptance acknowledgement reaches the browser.
first_check: Compare original input UUIDs, frozen bodies, acceptance timing and retained user rows rather than counting only transport sends.
handling: Implemented: preserve the pending input identity through repeated sends and replay the original unknown body; backend acceptance enforces immutable semantics.
avoid: Do not mint a fresh UUID per retry or deduplicate by text hash, which conflates intentional identical messages.

title: An older answer stays green
symptom: The display shows an older eligible answer after a newer recorded result becomes expired, inapplicable or lacks delivery evidence.
first_check: Distinguish a newer pending input without results from a newer recorded result; inspect original delivery and current observation times.
handling: Implemented: stop fallback after selecting a newer recorded result and recheck applicability after cleanup; historical facts remain retained.
avoid: Do not hide newer unusable state behind an older green answer or let a cached badge authorize a booking action.

title: Capacity blocks receipt recovery
symptom: The retained store is full and clients cannot discover whether their earlier commands committed before acknowledgements were lost.
first_check: Verify original-identity lookup occurs before new-work capacity and expiry checks, while catalog and credential validation still run.
handling: Implemented: original replay bypasses the selected new-identity capacity checks; it consumes no replacement identity. Separate authentication, transport and I/O capacity can still fail.
avoid: Do not delete protected identities to free display space or replace an unresolved original command with another business identity.

title: Timeout leaves unexpected capacity pressure
symptom: Clients time out, yet later requests still encounter capacity and underlying threads, sockets or remote work remain active.
first_check: Inspect actual retained tasks, process groups and writer owners; compare them with cancelled waiters before assuming a resource leak.
handling: Implemented: keep slots until actual work settles; retry incomplete close observations, with terminal peer-reset closure handled separately.
avoid: Do not release capacity in a waiter-level finally or assume cancelled await, elapsed timeout and reaped process mean the same thing.

title: Normal stop consumes pending inputs
symptom: A normal joined shutdown keeps dispatch claiming against closing Parent endpoints, potentially exhausting pending inputs or stranding the final room input.
first_check: Inspect dispatch admission, endpoint closure, room binding revocation and actual worker drainage in one shutdown dependency timeline.
handling: Open 0048 findings: quiescing dispatch before endpoint closure and correcting room retirement order are proposed repairs requiring implementation and fresh evidence.
avoid: Do not describe these lifecycle findings as solved or erase pending identities merely because launcher processes have exited.

title: A known receipt meets failed cleanup
symptom: A complete validated acknowledgement arrives, then writer cleanup raises and the caller is tempted to repeat the accepted command.
first_check: Check whether decoding completed before cleanup, preserve the exact receipt and inspect the retained writer and pending owner count.
handling: Implemented: preserve a decoded receipt through the declared ordinary close-error path while retaining incomplete cleanup. Later close observes settlement without resending; cancellation remains distinct control flow.
avoid: Do not let teardown failure overwrite a valid receipt or declare a resource free merely because domain decoding succeeded.

title: Eager scheduling hides a late owner
symptom: Shutdown appears complete before an eagerly started scan publishes its Task reference, leaving work or inspection resources arriving afterward.
first_check: Use the existing reentrant task-factory test to inspect publication reservation, actual scan count and close ordering before task creation returns.
handling: Implemented: reserve the publication Future before spawning and resolve it in finally; close waits for publication before draining actual owners.
avoid: Do not infer absence from an unset Task field or assume default scheduler ordering is guaranteed across task factories.

title: One unavailable result blocks later work
symptom: A transient feed, result or delivery read error prevents later useful events from progressing through completion processing.
first_check: Check per-row unavailable classification, separate discovery and terminal-ACK cursors, and the shared eight-row budget across cursor wrap.
handling: Implemented: leave transiently unavailable rows unacknowledged while bounded discovery examines later useful work; preserve identities and explicit pending observations.
avoid: Do not terminally acknowledge unknown rows to advance a watermark or reset the row budget when wrapping the cursor.

title: Schema validation itself causes effects
symptom: Opening a client evaluates unexpected metadata behavior, or an upgrade encounters unmanaged running work that cannot satisfy the new lease contract.
first_check: Inspect metadata relation kind before selecting its version, then verify owner role, ACTIVE state and unresolved legacy execution ownership.
handling: Implemented: catalog preflight rejects side-effecting metadata views; coordination upgrade refuses unmanaged running inquiries before DDL so original reconciliation can finish.
avoid: Do not adopt drifted metadata automatically, repair consent during startup or force an upgrade past unresolved legacy supplier work.
